# LocalXiv 0.0.16
Read arXiv papers comfortably on your Mac, then take them to Kindle. This preview finds a paper from its title, author, or topic, opens on Home with the papers you read last, and converts more papers through the Pandoc route.
## Changes
- **Paper search.** The home field accepts a title, an author, or a topic as well as a link. Suggestions show under the field while you type: papers already in your library first, then arXiv papers. Press Enter to open a results page with up to 5 library matches and 20 arXiv results. Results come from Semantic Scholar first, with arXiv as the backup. A link or a bare arXiv ID such as `1706.03762` imports at once, without a search. Settings has a Paper search section with a switch for suggestions and an optional Semantic Scholar API key. Without a key, searches share a public limit and fall back to arXiv. - **Home.** The app opens on Home, not on the sample paper, and lists the last three papers you opened under the field. Setup opens once, on the first launch. The Overview and Blog tabs show only when AI is connected and the view exists or is being made. **Explain this paper** in the sidebar starts them. Without a model and key, the server refuses the request instead of queueing a job that fails. - **Stage retry.** A failed Overview or Blog stage runs once more from the results of the stages before it, so one bad response no longer fails the whole job. The progress line says "second try". A cancelled job or a rejected key does not retry. - **Equations in figures.** Overview and Blog figures typeset subscripts and superscripts, and draw each equation in a math font inside a faint box on one line, in the text colour. Saved Overviews keep their old render until you regenerate them. - **Paper reader.** Display equations are centred, numbered as in the source, and bracket pairs around a fraction stretch to its height. Title footnotes stay ahead of the abstract's own marks. A notice before the title, such as the arXiv reproduction license, moves after the abstract instead of opening it. - **Blog.** The article opens with a generated title. Older Blogs show the plan's question. - **Navigation.** The macOS app menu has About and Settings items. The Library button clears when you open a paper. The Settings label **Language** is now **Tone**. - **Recommendations.** The recommendation job kept failing, so the app no longer queues it or shows it on Home. - **Parser.** On a frozen corpus of 100 arXiv papers from 68 templates, the Pandoc route converts 47 of the 98 papers with TeX source. Before this release it converted 27. No paper changed route for the worse, and no paper that kept its route changed its output. The fixes cover the equation fallback, which now reads the paper's own macros and the `physics` package, three Pandoc 3.11 stops (`\qed`, a bare `\input`, and `\href` before a line break), `algpseudocode` procedures and loops, `\subfigure` panels and redefined float environments, missing TeX system inputs, citation keys with `+`, `&`, or `@`, citations to missing bibliography entries, imsart, REVTeX, and MNRAS bibliographies, and labels that start with a digit. The number of papers with no EPUB fell from 37 to 33, including two PDF-only papers that have no EPUB by design.
The test suite now runs whole components through their public entry points instead of unit tests of private helpers. `tools/robustness/corpus.py` converts the frozen corpus at the working tree and at a base commit, and reports each failure with the pass, file, and line that caused it. See the [parser improvements report](../verification/2026-09-30-parser_improvements_intermediate.md).
## Verification and limitations
The release workflow checks the source, builds the portable app, runs native renderer tests, and verifies the packaged runtime after moving the app. Attached assets include the verification report, runtime inventory, exact app source, dependency source inputs, and SHA-256 checksums.
Local verification ran 55 component tests and 1 front-end test. All passed. One live test, which calls Semantic Scholar and arXiv, was skipped. The parser numbers come from the corpus run at `d71bc8e` against the branch point. No live pilot of Overview or Blog generation ran on this release build.
Open items:
- 51 papers in the corpus still fail on the Pandoc route and fall back to arXiv HTML or to the retained PDF. The report lists each cause. - Blog citations such as "[p00017]" are removed from the article, so a claim cannot be checked against the paper by a click. - The Overview figure is too small to read at phone width. - From 0.0.14: a review finding on an accepted figure can spend the figure's remaining budget on a redraw that fails a limit by one character.
Offline tests use scripted provider responses. They verify recovery and export behavior, not live-provider reliability, scientific accuracy, generation speed, or cost.
AI explanations remain experimental. Generation may take several minutes or fail, and generated claims need checking against the paper. AI requests send selected paper content and, where applicable, images to your configured provider and may incur charges. Paper search sends the typed text to Semantic Scholar and arXiv. Importing, reading, and exporting papers do not require AI credentials.
## Installation
Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 26 or newer. Download the DMG and drag LocalXiv into Applications. Finish active jobs before updating. Your library and settings remain on your Mac. Updater-enabled builds can use **LocalXiv → Check for Updates…** once the signed feed is published.
This preview is ad hoc signed, without Apple Developer ID signing or notarization. macOS may block the first launch. The Sparkle update feed is signed separately with the project's local update key. Separate-Mac installation and actual Kindle delivery are not covered by the automated checks.
